definitions.gloss: either way; in any case; regardless; no matter which
definitions.explanation: Used to indicate that the outcome or conclusion remains the same regardless of which option is chosen. Functions as a sentence-initial or mid-sentence connector.

examples.japanese: どちらにしても{行|い}かなければならない。
examples.english: Either way, I have to go.

examples.japanese: どちらにしても{結果|けっか}は{同|おな}じだと{思|おも}う。
examples.english: I think the result will be the same either way.

examples.japanese: {賛成|さんせい}でも{反対|はんたい}でも、どちらにしても{今日中|きょうじゅう}に{結論|けつろん}を{出|だ}さなければならない。
examples.english: Whether you're for it or against it, either way we have to reach a conclusion by the end of today.

notes:
A common conversational connector used to move a discussion forward when the specific choice between options does not matter. Often appears at the beginning of a sentence to shift focus to what remains constant regardless of the options.

FORMS:
- どちらにせよ: slightly more formal variant
- どっちにしても: casual variant using どっち
- いずれにしても: more formal equivalent

COMMON PATTERNS:
- AでもBでも、どちらにしても〜: whether A or B, either way ~
- どちらにしても{変|か}わらない: it doesn't change either way

SIMILAR WORDS:
- いずれにしても: in any case — more formal, used in writing and formal speech
- どっちにしろ: either way — casual, slightly blunt
- とにかく: anyway, in any case — shifts topic rather than comparing options
